Mauricio Pochettino, manager of Manchester United, reacts during the Premier League at Liverpool [Michael Regan/Getty Images]By Kevin HandPublished On 22 Nov 202622 Nov 2026
If Mauricio Pochettino had any doubt about the size of the job in front of him at Manchester United, his players confirmed his worst fears within 13 minutes of his first game in charge – a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.
As the home side surged into a two-goal lead in the opening exchanges at Anfield, with the away side reduced to 10 men, the sinking sensation for United – who are second bottom of the Premier League – immediately returned.

Any ‘new-manager bounce’, as feared by Reds manager Andoni Iraola, had no time to materialise with a rash challenge from Lenny Yoro on Alexander Isak leading to a straight red in the eighth minute.
The resulting free-kick was powered home by Dominik Szoboszlai, with Florian Wirtz thereafter converting a sharp attack in a flash – ending the match as a contest.
Pochettino slammed the decision to send off Yoro after the game, but there was a familiar feeling about the performance overall.
Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at five key takeaways as the opening salvo of the ninth manager since United’s last league title in 2013 fell apart – resulting in the worst start for a new manager of the club in 100 years.

item.title: Cockroaches, dissent and a paradigm shift in India
item.description:
play video
play video
Video Duration 25 minutes 15 seconds play-arrow
25:15
The rise of Cockroach Janta Party and what it reveals about the future of politics and journalism in India.Read more
A youth-led movement born as online satire has unsettled Indian politics. Named after a dismissive remark by the chief justice, the Cockroach Janta Party has mobilised some of the country’s biggest protests in years. They have been driven by anger over exam leaks, unemployment and a lack of political accountability.
The demonstrators have been met by heavy police crackdowns and clashed with mainstream media outlets they accuse of serving the government.
As young Indians turn to social media and independent outlets to tell their stories, this film examines the growing divide between India’s youth and mainstream media and what it could mean for the future of politics and journalism.
Contributors:
Manisha Pande – Editorial director, Newslaundry
Ashutosh Ranka – Co-convenor, Cockroach Janta Party
Rajat Sethi – Visiting fellow, India Foundation
Priyanshi Sharma – Cofounder, Peek TVPublished On 22 Nov 202622 Nov 2026

Kawas stands on Steinway Street in Astoria, Queens, New York, on October 8, 2026 [Hannah Raslan/Al Jazeera]By Hannah RaslanPublished On 22 Nov 202622 Nov 2026
New York City, United States – “You have all elected the first Palestinian in New York Senate history!” Aber Kawas shouted over cheers to hundreds of Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) members at a bar on election night.
As chants of “Aber! Aber! Aber!” filled the patio of Bohemia Beer Garden on November 3, media cameras flashed against her shiny blazer, embroidered with traditional Palestinian tatreez in gold and red.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3New York Democratic Socialists urge Ocasio-Cortez to run for US presidentlist 2 of 3London Palestine Film Festival returns for 27th yearlist 3 of 3What does Israel’s new ground offensive mean for Palestinians in Gaza?end of list
Kawas, 34, made history as the first Palestinian, and the first Muslim woman, in the New York state Senate and the state legislature. She won the seat representing district 12 in northwest Queens, home to one of New York City’s largest Arab communities, where nearly half of residents were born outside the United States.
As her speech ended and chants of “Free, Free Palestine” rang through the garden, Stylianos Karolidis, a DSA organiser on Kawas’s team, stepped up to remind supporters that she really, really had not wanted to run for office. The DSA had to “hound her non-stop” until she acquiesced, he said.

The arrests at the Seattle-Tacoma international airport prompted protests on Saturday night [File: Lindsey Wasson/AP]By Catherine NouhanPublished On 22 Nov 202622 Nov 2026
Democrats and state officials have denounced a now-viral immigration arrest in Washington state, which took place on an airport jet bridge as passengers were boarding a flight to Los Angeles.
“What we’ve seen happening in Washington is atrocious,” said Nevada’s Governor-elect Aaron Ford, a Democrat, in an interview with the news outlet MS NOW on Sunday.

He added that he supported safeguards to restrict the actions taken by United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents.
“ We need some control over these vigilante ICE agents who come en masse in terrorising neighbourhoods, at airports included,” Ford said.
The two arrests unfolded on Saturday morning at Seattle-Tacoma international airport, as passengers boarded Alaska Airlines Flight 1306.
Videos recorded by passengers showed immigration agents in masks surrounding a man and a woman on the narrow jet bridge, forcing them to the ground as other travellers looked on.
Passengers could be heard asking the officers to identify themselves, while a woman repeatedly shouted that she and her family had work permits.
In one video, a young girl can be heard screaming as officers remove a man through a side door. In another part of the footage, an officer appeared to shove a bystander who tried to intervene.

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino reacts [Ian Hodgson/Reuters]By Alexander HoadPublished On 22 Nov 202622 Nov 2026
Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start to his Manchester United reign as the 10-man Red Devils were humbled 4-0 by old rivals Liverpool at Anfield Stadium.
Leny Yoro’s red card eight minutes in set the tone as Andoni Iraola’s side raced into a 2-0 lead after just 13 minutes and spurned a host of chances before adding to their advantage after the break.

United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions – the most of any top-flight team in any of Europe’s major leagues. But in truth, the hosts could well have matched, or even surpassed, their famous 7-0 victory in 2023 in this fixture.
Pochettino’s side sit 19th, a point off the bottom of the table, in English football’s Premier League, with eight points from 11 games. Meanwhile, the Reds are up to fourth, seven points behind leaders Arsenal.
Liverpool were already well on top when the game turned after eight minutes as Matthijs de Ligt – who struggled throughout after being handed his first Premier League start in 357 days in Pochettino’s first selection – was caught out by a long ball down the left channel which allowed Alexander Isak to race towards goal.
